articles.title: Streaming MySQL to BigQuery with the binlog: how CDC works, and the parts that bite
articles.excerpt: Most teams start syncing MySQL to BigQuery with a nightly dump or a query like SELECT * FROM orders WHERE updated_at > :last_run. It works until someone asks why deleted orders still show up in the da…
articles.body: Most teams start syncing MySQL to BigQuery with a nightly dump or a query like SELECT * FROM orders WHERE updated_at > :last_run . It works until someone asks why deleted orders still show up in the dashboard, or why yesterday's numbers changed. This post walks through how log-based change data capture (CDC) from MySQL to BigQuery works end to end, and the details that decide whether it's correct and affordable. Disclosure: I build Quayen , a managed MySQL to BigQuery CDC service. Everything here applies whether you build this yourself with Debezium or use any managed tool. Why polling isn't enough Query-based syncs on an updated_at column have three structural problems: Deletes are invisible.

articles.title: CVE-2026-109518: The APT Verification Bypass and What to Do About It
articles.excerpt: A package manager is a trust machine. When apt installs a package, it is supposed to verify cryptographic signatures and checksums before anything runs. CVE-2026-109518 breaks that assumption: a craft…
articles.body: A package manager is a trust machine. When apt installs a package, it is supposed to verify cryptographic signatures and checksums before anything runs. CVE-2026-109518 breaks that assumption: a crafted package can convince a vulnerable APT to skip verification and install anyway. What the flaw does APT validates packages with GPG signatures and SHA-256 checksums. The vulnerability sits in the verification logic itself. By manipulating package metadata — the descriptor that tells APT what it is about to install — an attacker can trigger a path where the verification routine exits early or accepts a placeholder validation result.
articles.author: Gurveer Singh

articles.title: Dedicated IP vs shared IP: what’s the difference?
articles.excerpt: When you connect through a VPN, a proxy or a hosting provider, the websites you visit don't see your address. They see the provider's. So the useful question isn't "do I have an IP?", it's "how many o…
articles.body: When you connect through a VPN, a proxy or a hosting provider, the websites you visit don't see your address. They see the provider's. So the useful question isn't "do I have an IP?", it's "how many other people appear behind the same IP?" That is the whole difference between a shared IP and a dedicated IP. This post walks through what each one means, the trade-offs, a few common myths, and a quick way to decide. TL;DR Shared IP Dedicated IP Who uses the address Many customers One customer Does it stay the same?

The change confirms our October report about Android 10 users receiving warnings that support was ending. Phones stuck on Android 9 or 10 are no longer officially supported, with affected users already reporting that Android Auto has stopped working. Every few years, Google raises the bar for the oldest Android versions that can still run Android Auto . Android 6 lost its place in 2022, followed by Android 8 in 2024 . Now, two more versions are reaching the end of the road, and Google has officially confirmed Android 11 as the new minimum requirement for wired Android Auto connections.

articles.body: Some science fiction franchises are so ambitious they become their own cinematic languages. Star Wars built an entire galaxy with a mythology that’s still growing almost 50 years later, while Blade Runner helped define the vision of a far-future Los Angeles through rampant tech advancement and unchecked capitalism. They’re the kinds of franchises that can change the way we imagine the future, influencing everything from fashion and technology to the stories other filmmakers want to tell. Plenty of franchises have tried to capture that same vibe, but few have managed to pull it off quite like The Matrix .

articles.excerpt: On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. Here's why Venus Express mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this.

articles.title: Who is King Ghidorah? The cosmic connections of Godzilla Minus Zero's foe
articles.excerpt: Godzilla will go toe-to-toe with long-time foe King Ghidorah in Godzilla Minus Zero. This three-headed Kaiju's origins aren't just space-based; one of the largest structures in the universe shares its…
articles.body: Godzilla goes toe-to-toe with long-time foe King Ghidorah in Godzilla Minus Zero, which opened in theaters on Friday (Nov. 6). Though the three-headed golden Kaiju might seem like a natural native of Monster Island, King Ghidorah actually emerged from the depths of space. However, it isn't just the origins of King Ghidorah — also known as Monster Zero in the Godzilla movie Invasion of Astro-Monster (1965) — that are this beast's only cosmic connection. One of the largest structures in the universe, the King Ghidorah Supercluster , was named in honor of Godzilla's primary antagonist. Eat that, King Kong!

articles.body: If you follow the EV industry in North America, you’d be forgiven for thinking that the future of transportation revolves around electric SUVs and pickups. Every week seems to bring another teaser from a startup promising to reinvent the family car or truck. The latest electric SUVs, “coming soon” tiny trucks, lifestyle trucks, modular trucks, etc. Companies like Slate, TELO, and countless others have generated plenty of excitement, even if many of them still have everything left to prove. Don’t get me wrong – I hope they succeed. We need more affordable electric vehicles.
